messages:
IncidentBot: Pager — High eviction_rate on us-west-1/gpu-pool (sev-2) :rotating_light:

Kim: seeing this, grabbing it. looks like eviction spiked after a deployment + high LLM chat traffic.

Kim: quick check — are customers seeing 5xx or just latency? sam can you pull support queue?

Sam: Maya flagged 3 customers with increased 5xx around 15:03 UTC, support ticket IDs #8452 #8459 #8461. brief user errors: transient inference timeout 504s.

Kim: thanks. that's customer impact > sev-2. I'm going to open an incident channel and do a handoff if I need to step out.

Jon: pinging from home — oncall takeover in 8m if needed. Kim if you want me to own mitigation steps I can.

Kim: handing off to Jon — I'm going to run a quick eviction histogram and check batch sizing. Jon please coordinate alert tuning afterwards.

Jon: acknowledged. first pass: shard eviction_count is 3x baseline, queue depth > 200 for a minute. suspects: bursty traffic + small batch window causing KV thrash.

Lex: chiming in — we rolled kernel patch 2 deployments back that changed KV retention heuristics. could be compounding with the burst.

Jon: plan in next 10m: 1) temporarily increase eviction threshold for evict_alert to reduce paging noise, 2) enable per-pool soft-cap to shed best-effort traffic, 3) failover some routes to fallback model variant (lower mem).

Jon: applying temporary alert change now (will revert after post-incident review).

Jon: alert change diff:

```yaml
# alert_rules/eviction_rate.yaml (temp tweak)
- alert: HighEvictionRate
  expr: eviction_rate > 5.0 # was 2.0
  for: 2m # was 1m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall/evictions
```

Maya: noted that we should annotate runbook with customer IDs and support ticket links. I'll add them.

Kim: good. also create a dashboard panel for eviction_count by model and pool. we kept missing that granularity earlier.

Lex: created a draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/evictions/eviction-debug — it has per-pool, per-model heatmap. sharing to eng-oncall.

Sam: I've updated support tickets with incident link + temporary mitigation notes. customers notified that we're rolling out mitigations.

Jon: executing controlled route fallback now — shifting 12% of traffic off primary variant to lite-quant model. watching error rates.

IncidentBot: RouteFailover executed by Jon at 15:12:18 UTC — 12% traffic shifted to model-lite-q/v1.

Jon: within 5m error rate dropped for the affected customers from 3.2% -> 0.6% and eviction_count trending down. good signal.

Kim: thanks everyone. action items post-incident: 1) revert temporary alert threshold change only after we confirm stable for 48h, 2) add owner and annotation to evictions runbook (owner: Lex), 3) create a permanent alert tuning PR with reasoning + test harness, 4) add dashboard panel to default oncall view, 5) write post-incident note with customer impact summary.

Lex: I'll take #2 and #3. PR placeholder: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-alerts/pulls/213 — will include test sims and threshold rationale.

Jon: I'll own #1 and monitoring for 48h. also will add an automatic alert squelch rule to avoid paging during short bursts (squelch window 3m after known deploy).

Maya: I'll consolidate customer impact and add to the postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood/internal/incidents/1805123456 — will include ticket links and customer comms.

Sam: recommend we also add a synthetic test that simulates 1.5x batch bursts per pool to catch this in pre-prod. I'll coordinate with QA.

Kim: agreed. final note: update runbook link to include explicit rollback/playbook snippet and owner sections (owner: Lex, backup: Jon).

Jon: closing live mitigation. leaving a TODO to revert the alert change in the infra-alerts repo once stable.

IncidentBot: Incident marked as resolved (mitigated) at 15:28:50 UTC — follow-up review scheduled 2026-03-16 17:00 UTC in #postmortems.

Kim: thanks all :thumbsup: — moving this into a formal post-incident review.
